title: Pull-Up Footwork: Hop vs 1-2
description: Players compare the two pull-up stops — the two-foot hop and the 1-2 step — from each direction, learning when each one keeps them square and in rhythm.

content.objective: Stop from the dribble into a balanced shot with both footwork patterns and know which suits each direction.
content.setup: Lines at both wings at the three-point line.
content.organization: Alternate patterns each rep; switch wings.
instructions: Drive toward the middle with the outside hand.
Hop: gather the ball and land on both feet together, then shoot.
Next rep, 1-2: land inside foot then outside foot, then shoot.
Note which stop feels more balanced in each direction.
coachingPoints: Hop: both feet land together, square on landing.
1-2: inside foot first turns the body.
Last dribble hard to stop the momentum.
commonMistakes: Landing with the feet too close together.
Travelling between the gather and the shot.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
successCriteria: Lands within half a metre of the take-off spot.
content.gameApplication: Shooters who can stop both ways pull up in rhythm from any direction.
